body.statement: If \(D_t(a)=0\) almost surely for both arms, then for every \(\Delta_T\geq0\), the actual hidden-tail bias satisfies \(b_{T,\Delta}=0\), \(U_{a,\Delta}=0\), and \(\widehat\tau_{T,\Delta}\) reduces to the difference of independent fixed-quota arm means. On the regular class, \(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm W}\) is pointwise asymptotically honest for this prompt-delay law. The generic envelope radius \(B_{T,\Delta}=2\min\{1,L(1+h_{T,\Delta})^{-\beta}\}\) need not equal zero under this specialization; the generic Gaussian branch reduces asymptotically to ordinary Wald only along sequences for which \(B_{T,\Delta}/\widehat s_{T,\Delta}\to0\), in which case \(c_\eta(B_{T,\Delta}/\widehat s_{T,\Delta})\to z_{1-\eta/2}\).
body.justification: The reduction separates the zero actual bias of a prompt-delay law from the possibly positive conservative radius retained by the generic envelope-based procedure.
body.gap: This is a required compatibility check rather than a novelty claim.
body.consumer: Implementers can use ordinary fixed-quota Wald inference for a certified prompt-delay law and can identify when the generic envelope-based Gaussian branch remains conservatively padded.
body.proof_tex:
Assume \(D_t(a)=0\) almost surely for both arms. Since \(g_{T,\Delta}\geq0\) and \(h_{T,\Delta}\geq0\) for all sufficiently large \(T\), the definitions give
\[
 X_{a,j}^{\Delta}=Y_{a,j},
 \qquad R_{a,j}^{\Delta}=0,
 \qquad U_{a,\Delta}=0.
\]
Moreover \(\mathbf 1\{D(a)>h_{T,\Delta}\}=0\), and hence \(b_{T,\Delta}=0\). On quota success,
\[
 \widehat\tau_{T,\Delta}=M_{1,\Delta}-M_{0,\Delta},
\]
a difference of two independent deterministic-prefix arm-tape means. On the regular class, the maximal normalized summand tends to zero by the quota orders and the variance floor. The characteristic-function calculation (4) and the sample-variance calculation (7)--(8) therefore give pointwise standard-normal studentization. Since quota failure has probability at most \(4T^{-4}\) and returns the full parameter interval, \(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm W}\) is pointwise asymptotically honest for this prompt-delay law.

The generic radius \(B_{T,\Delta}\) is a worst-case radius for the whole polynomial envelope; because \(L>0\), it need not vanish merely because the particular law has prompt delays. Continuity and strict monotonicity in the defining equation for \(c_\eta\) give
\[
 c_\eta(u)\longrightarrow c_\eta(0)=z_{1-\eta/2}
 \qquad\text{as }u\downarrow0.
\]
Thus, if \(B_{T,\Delta}/\widehat s_{T,\Delta}\to0\), the random critical value converges to the ordinary-Wald critical value. On a regular prompt-delay sequence, (12), (22), and variance consistency also give
\[
 d_{T,\Delta}/\widehat s_{T,\Delta}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Conversely, if \(B_{T,\Delta}/\widehat s_{T,\Delta}\) does not tend to zero, a subsequence stays bounded away from zero, and strict monotonicity gives a critical value bounded away from \(z_{1-\eta/2}\) on a further subsequence. Hence the generic Gaussian branch reduces to ordinary Wald asymptotically exactly under the displayed bias-ratio condition.
